questions.explain: The chapter's premise is that native vectors cover the majority of workloads, and the dedicated engines earn their place only at the workloads that genuinely outgrow the relational engine.
options: For most teams reading the book, SQL Server 2025 native vectors are enough; dedicated engines exist for workloads that genuinely outgrow the relational engine
Every team should start with a dedicated vector engine
SQL Server vectors are only suitable for prototypes
Both systems must always be deployed together
questions.q: What is the chapter's 'honest starting position' on the SQL Server vs. dedicated vector database decision?

questions.explain: Extreme scale with high throughput, complex filtered search at scale, first-class hybrid retrieval, and SaaS-scale multi-tenancy are the four situations named.
options: When the corpus is under 50,000 vectors
When vectors must join relational tables in the same query

Past tens of millions of vectors with hundreds or thousands of queries per second and strict p99 latency budgets, where specialized storage, quantization, and distributed architectures justify the cost
When the team has no DBA staff
questions.q: In which situation does the chapter say dedicated engines pull ahead of SQL Server native vectors?

questions.explain: Every write path must update two systems in the right order with failure handling; divergence is a matter of when, not if — and that engineering is permanent, with owners, runbooks, and on-call coverage.
options: The SaaS subscription bill

The synchronization pipeline between the system of record and the vector store — embedding generation, change propagation (CDC/triggers/app events), drift detection and reconciliation, a second security model, and coordinated DR
The cost of the GPU instances
The price of the embedding API calls
questions.q: What does the chapter call the most underestimated cost of a dedicated vector database?

questions.explain: The decision graph routes under ~5M vectors to SQL Server, 5M–50M by QPS/latency SLA (modest → SQL Server), and 50M+ to a dedicated engine.
options: A dedicated engine, because 20M is over 50K vectors
Chroma embedded mode
Exact VECTOR_DISTANCE search without any index
SQL Server native vectors — the 5M–50M band stays on SQL Server when QPS and SLAs are modest, with dedicated engines reserved for aggressive requirements
questions.q: According to the chapter's decision graph, a corpus of 20 million vectors with modest QPS and latency SLAs most likely maps to:

questions.explain: The vector store holds derived data — embeddings computed from documents — and derived data can always be rebuilt from the source, which simplifies every DR conversation and model migration.
options: Duplicate every collection in both systems for redundancy
Keep SQL Server as the system of record for source documents and treat every vector store as derived data that can always be rebuilt; each vector collection lives in exactly one system
Synchronize the two systems hourly regardless of changes
Store embeddings in SQL Server and documents in the vector database
questions.q: In a hybrid architecture (both SQL Server and a dedicated engine), what discipline does the chapter require?

title: When to Use SQL Server Vectors vs a Dedicated Vector Database
